articles.title: Pluralistic: IP can't save you from AI (18 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: 知识产权救不了你：AI 时代的劳工与隐私
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 版权无法保护创意工作者免受 AI 的工资侵蚀，劳工权利和隐私权才是根本。
paragraphs: 很多人认为，扩大版权、禁止 AI 抓取训练数据，就能保护创意工作者的利益。但作者认为这是必败的策略，因为版权从来没能给创作者带来真正的谈判筹码。
版权是假想的财产权，创作者靠它和媒体公司讨价还价。但垄断让少数巨头握有全部话语权，版权越扩张，老板越富，创作者越穷。
真正的力量来自劳工权利。编剧工会是靠罢工打败 AI 的，不是靠版权。但美国 1947 年的《塔夫脱-哈特利法》禁止了行业性集体谈判，让这条路变得困难。
更糟的是，版权诉讼根本不是为了保护你的工资。老板们起诉 AI 公司，赢了赔偿也进他们口袋，他们还想用 AI 替代你。
今天的例子：破产的 Spirit Airlines 把员工的所有数据卖给了 Google 用于 AI 训练。每个员工对邮件有版权，但「职务作品」条款让版权归公司所有。
2001 年安然公司破产时，员工邮件也被公开，成为「安然语料库」，至今仍困扰着 158 名员工。美国劳动法不保护雇主手中的个人信息。
所以，别幻想用「LLC+MFA」的个体户方式去谈判。要联合所有工人争取行业性集体谈判，联合所有消费者争取隐私权，这才是真正解决问题的权利。

en.thesis: Copyright cannot protect creative workers from AI-driven wage erosion; labor rights and privacy rights are the real answers.
paragraphs: Many think expanding copyright to ban AI scraping will protect creative workers. But the author argues this is a losing strategy, because copyright never gave creators real bargaining power.

Copyright is a pseudo-property right meant for bargaining with media companies. But monopoly concentrates power in a few giants; the more copyright expands, the richer the bosses and the poorer the creators.
Real power comes from labor rights. The writers' guild beat AI with a strike, not copyright. But the 1947 Taft-Hartley Act banned sectoral bargaining, making that route hard.
Worse, copyright lawsuits aren't meant to protect your wages. Bosses sue AI companies, but any winnings go to them, and they still want to replace you with AI.

Today's example: bankrupt Spirit Airlines sold all employee data to Google for AI training. Every employee has copyright in their emails, but 'works made for hire' clauses give ownership to the company.
When Enron collapsed in 2001, employee emails became the 'Enron Corpus,' still haunting 158 employees. US labor law doesn't protect personal information in the employer's hands.
So don't fantasize about the 'LLC with an MFA' approach. Join all workers to demand sectoral bargaining, and all consumers to demand privacy rights — that's the real fix.

articles.title: A joke domain purchase turned in geopolitical warfare
articles.titleZh: 一个玩笑域名的购买演变成地缘政治战争
articles.author: kareiva

zh.thesis: 一个业余的气象气球追踪服务，无意中绘制了军事地点，并卷入了间谍气球事件和乌克兰战争。
paragraphs: 2018 年，有人注册了一个域名 sondehub.org，只是把它重定向到现有的气象气球追踪网站。这原本是个玩笑，但后来他们发现业余追踪者太少，而官方的气象气球数据又不够，于是决定自己开始收集数据。
他们的系统能追踪气球一直到落地，这比官方软件更精确。他们还开发了「反向预测」系统，从已经升空的气球数据反推发射地点，结果意外发现了很多未记录的军事发射点。
军方对此很敏感，要求他们不要在地图上标出这些点。他们同意了，但数据仍然公开。
2023 年发生了「中国间谍气球」事件，他们的网站流量暴增，还收到了来自美国军方和航空部门的请求。这让他们意识到，自己的数据可能被用于导弹瞄准或无人机行动。
2024 年底，有人开始滥用他们的 API 进行大规模预测查询。他们怀疑这与乌克兰战争有关，可能涉及无人机打击。他们没有阻断访问，而是尽力保持服务稳定，并提供了本地运行的方案。
期间他们还收到了美国「战争部情报与安全办公室」的数据请求，但因为对方是军事机构且无社区益处，他们开了账单但对方没付。
除此之外，他们还遇到过各种奇怪的事件：飞机与气球的碰撞、寻找丢失气象气球的人、以及一个自称「芝士占卜师」的记者。这家原本是玩笑的服务，现在成了各方关注的焦点。

en.thesis: An amateur weather-balloon tracking service accidentally mapped military locations and got caught up in spy-balloon incidents and the Ukraine war.
paragraphs: In 2018 someone registered sondehub.org as a joke, redirecting it to a site that tracks weather balloons. But they soon found that amateurs tracked too few, and official data was incomplete, so they started collecting their own.

Their system tracked balloons all the way to the ground, which was more precise than official software. They also built a reverse-prediction system that inferred launch sites, and it turned up many undocumented military sites.
The military was sensitive about this and asked them not to mark such sites on maps. They agreed, but the data stayed public.

The 2023 'Chinese spy balloon' incident brought a traffic surge and requests from the US military and aviation authorities. It became clear their data could be used for missile targeting or drone operations.

In late 2024 someone started abusing their API with mass prediction queries. They suspected a link to the Ukraine war and drone strikes. They kept the service running, avoided blocking the source, and offered a local version.
They also got a data request from the US 'Office of the Secretary of War (Intelligence and Security)', but since it offered no community benefit, they sent an invoice that was never paid.
Along the way: a plane-balloon collision, someone looking for a lost radiosonde, and a writer who calls herself a 'Cheese Fortune Teller'. The joke service has become a hub of attention.

articles.title: Pluralistic: The ordinariness of evil (19 Aug 2026)
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 把 AI 说得极其邪恶，其实是在帮 AI 公司融资。
paragraphs: AI 老板们总在公开哀叹 AI 的可怕潜力，比如取代工作、觉醒毁灭人类。但这看似担忧的话，其实是在吹嘘 AI 的潜力。
现在的 AI 只是新奇的玩具，对熟练者有点用，价值相当于一个插件，可能有用也可能没用。它是个正常技术，但正常技术不值得一年一万亿美元的投资，以及裁员换 AI 的代价。
真正可怕的不是 AI 的潜力，而是它已经造成的破坏：浪费钱、烧水电排碳、摧毁就业和生产。这些破坏不会变成未来的好处，只会让 AI 公司把钱烧光，还搭上你的退休金。
所以我们不该跟着炒作 AI 的「邪恶」，而该把它当正常技术，该批判的是它的实际危害。AI 不会污染使用者，它只是电脑。
把 AI 说得极其邪恶，会把 Altman 之辈捧成超级反派，帮他们融资。这叫「criti-hype」——复述营销话术然后加一句「（这很糟）」。正确的做法是指出他们在撒谎。
所以关键是把 AI 当作正常技术，既不捧杀也不贬低，集中火力打击它的实际危害。

en.thesis: Portraying AI as exceptionally evil actually helps AI companies raise money.
paragraphs: AI bosses keep publicly lamenting AI's terrible potential, like taking jobs and awakening to destroy humanity. But this seemingly worried talk is really boasting about AI's potential.

Current AI is a novelty toy, somewhat useful to skilled practitioners, worth about as much as a plugin. It's a normal technology, but normal technologies don't deserve a trillion dollars a year in investment and mass firings to replace workers with AI.

What is truly scary is not AI's potential but the damage it already does: wasting money, burning water and electricity, emitting carbon, destroying jobs and production. This damage won't turn into future benefits; it will just burn through AI companies' cash and eat your retirement savings.
So instead of amplifying AI's 'evil', we should treat it as a normal technology and criticize its actual harms. AI doesn't poison its users; it's just computers.

Portraying AI as exceptionally evil elevates the likes of Altman to super-villain status and helps them raise money. This is 'criti-hype' — repeating marketing claims and then adding '(and that's bad)'. The right move is to point out that they are lying.
The key is to treat AI as normal, neither boosting nor demonizing it, and focus fire on its actual harms.

articles.title: Why I'm Staying Out Of The Substack Religion Debate
articles.titleZh: 为什么我不参与 Substack 上的宗教大辩论
articles.author: Scott Alexander

zh.thesis: 作者的不信神不是基于精细推理，而是基于一种前理性的直觉，类似于对“外星人帮助拿破仑”式说法的不假思索的排除。
paragraphs: 最近 Substack 上掀起了一波关于上帝存在的辩论，Matthew Adelstein 和 Richard Chappell 等人纷纷下场。这让人想起 2000 年代早期的在线无神论热潮，如今它又回来了，势头不减。作者当年乐在其中，现在却提不起兴趣。
他的不信神感不是来自对微调论证、奇迹论证等细节的推敲，而是先于这些论证。就像一个社会如果认真讨论“外星人是否帮助了拿破仑崛起”，我们不会去逐条计算证据，而是凭常识直接排除。
这种“荒谬启发式”很危险，它曾在 1900 年排除核武器，在 1850 年排除重于空气的飞行器。但它对不信神者很有效，对信神者却毫无说服力。所以更深的问题是：为什么我们会排除“外星人助拿破仑”这种说法？
答案是过拟合。“强大隐形实体特意促成此事”能解释一切，但比任何具体解释都差，因为它可以适应任何证据。我们对这类理论有先验的惩罚，也就是所说的“阴谋论”。外星人版本更糟，它避开了人类阴谋的破绽——比如记忆清除技术——让惩罚无用武之地。
作者承认这套论述有点“伪知识分子”，但他觉得人们的主观直觉不可靠。他试图回应一个常见的辩解：上帝是无限简单的存在，所以不受惩罚。但“减去限制”的诡辩是偷换概念，减去否定等于增加，照此逻辑造星舰应比造双翼机容易，而两岁小孩的画也比米开朗基罗的更高明。
上帝简单论还依赖“心物二元论”，认为心智有非物理的“奇异基板”。但计算并不神秘：神经科学、药物、基因、睡眠和 AI 都证明计算发生在普通大脑上。即使意识可能有奇异基板，那也换不来无限计算力。
所以作者的结论是：有神论与“外星人助拿破仑”同属一类，应当被先验排除，而不是被精细论证击败。这正是他对辩论提不起兴趣的原因。当然，这篇“不参与”的声明本身，也是一种参与。

en.thesis: The author's atheism rests not on fine-grained reasoning but on a pre-rational intuition, akin to how we unthinkingly dismiss claims like 'aliens helped Napoleon.'
paragraphs: Substack recently hosted a wave of debates about God's existence, with Matthew Adelstein, Richard Chappell, and many others joining in. It feels like the early-2000s online atheism craze has returned, nearly as strong as ever. The author enjoyed it back then, but now finds it uninteresting.

His lack of belief doesn't stem from weighing the details of fine-tuning or miracle arguments; it precedes them. Consider a society where people seriously debate whether aliens helped Napoleon's rise. We wouldn't compute the Bayesian evidence; we'd dismiss it outright by common sense.

This 'absurdity heuristic' is dangerous—it would have ruled out nuclear weapons in 1900 and heavier-than-air flight in 1850. It works for atheists, but fails to convince believers. So the real question is: why do we exclude 'aliens caused Napoleon'?

The answer is overfitting. A 'powerful hidden entity intended this specific outcome' can explain anything, but it's worse than any concrete explanation because it adapts to all evidence. We impose a preemptive penalty on such theories—that's what we call conspiracy theories. The alien version is worse, dodging the usual pitfalls of human conspiracies, like memory-wipe tech, making the penalty toothless.

The author admits his argument feels a bit 'midwit,' but says intuition can't be trusted. He tackles one common defense: God is infinitely simple, so He's exempt. But the 'subtracting limits' trick is a sleight of hand—subtracting negatives is adding. By that logic, building a starship should be easier than a biplane, and a toddler's scribble better than Michelangelo.

Divine simplicity also relies on dualism, positing an exotic substrate for mind. But computation isn't mysterious: neuroscience, drugs, genes, sleep, and AI all show it happens on ordinary brains. Even if consciousness needs an exotic substrate, it won't buy infinite computation.

So theism, like 'aliens caused Napoleon,' deserves preemptive dismissal, not fine-grained refutation. That's why the author finds the debate uninteresting. Of course, this very post is itself a participation in the debate.

articles.title: What Happens If OpenAI Dies?
articles.titleZh: 如果 OpenAI 死了会怎样？
articles.author: Ed Zitron

zh.thesis: OpenAI 的财务状况不可持续，其崩溃的可能性被严重低估。
paragraphs: OpenAI 正处于危险境地。过去一个月里，它完成了 70 亿美元的股票回购，同时首席运营官和首席营收官相继离职，后者上任仅八个月。
它的营收增长正在放缓，而竞争对手 Anthropic 正在以更快的速度增长。OpenAI 2025 年营收 130.7 亿美元，亏损 209 亿美元，烧钱速度惊人。
OpenAI 承诺了巨额计算开支，预计到 2030 年需要超过 800 亿美元。它每年需要融资 1000 亿到 2000 亿美元，但资金来源正在枯竭。
软银已无力再投资，英伟达表示可能不再追加，亚马逊自身的自由现金流也为负。OpenAI 的估值过高，IPO 前景不明，难以吸引新资本。
如果 OpenAI 崩溃，将冲击整个 AI 行业，影响微软、谷歌、亚马逊等巨头的云收入，甚至可能拖垮软银和英伟达。
作者呼吁认真对待这一风险，认为 OpenAI 的死亡不是会不会发生的问题，而是何时发生的问题。

en.thesis: OpenAI's finances are unsustainable and its collapse is far more likely than most admit.
paragraphs: OpenAI is in a precarious position. In the past month, it completed a $7 billion share buyback while its COO and CRO both resigned, the latter after only eight months on the job.
Its revenue growth is decelerating while rival Anthropic grows faster. OpenAI lost $20.9 billion in 2025 on $13.07 billion in revenue, burning cash at an alarming rate.
OpenAI has made enormous compute commitments, requiring over $800 billion by 2030. It needs to raise $100-200 billion every year, but funding sources are drying up.

SoftBank can't invest more, NVIDIA says its investment may be the last, and Amazon has negative free cash flow. OpenAI's valuation is inflated, its IPO prospects dim, making it hard to attract new capital.
If OpenAI collapses, it would ripple through the entire AI industry, hitting cloud revenues of Microsoft, Google, and Amazon, and potentially dragging down SoftBank and NVIDIA.
The author urges taking this risk seriously, arguing that OpenAI's death is a matter of when, not if.

articles.title: I Was Compelled to Revisit: Rory Kennedy on “Freefall: A Reckoning For Boeing”
articles.titleZh: 我不得不重访：罗里·肯尼迪谈《自由落体：波音的清算》
articles.author: Nell Minow

zh.thesis: 波音至今没有为 346 条人命真正负责，利润优先于安全的文化依然在延续。
paragraphs: 罗里·肯尼迪在《坠落：波音案》之后拍了续集《自由落体：波音的清算》。前一部聚焦两起相隔五个月的 737 MAX 坠机，346 人遇难。波音先推给飞行员，最后承认是 MCAS（飞行稳定用的机动特性增强系统）的问题。
但肯尼迪说，飞机复飞后怪事接连不断：引擎掉落、客舱冒烟、轮子失灵，还有阿拉斯加航空的舱门飞脱。为前作作证的吹哨人约翰·巴尼特在作证期间蹊跷死亡，更多吹哨人私下找她，说「你得看看波音内部」。
新片更多进入工厂，从吹哨人视角展示波音的现状。肯尼迪对比了 1985 年日航坠机后社长高木养根挨家挨户登门道歉，而波音至今没有给许多遇难者家属打过一个道歉电话。
影片进一步挖了杰克·韦尔奇式管理模式的毒害：股东利益压倒一切，CEO 拿上亿美元薪酬，和业绩无关。短期压成本，长期却持续亏损——专家说这家公司正在自我毁灭。
肯尼迪说，她希望波音能活下来，回到造最安全飞机的时代。但改变需要行动：换一个工程师出身的 CEO，司法部真的起诉问责，给 FAA 拨款并防止旋转门。选举在即，选民该看看候选人支不支持监管机构。

en.thesis: Boeing has yet to truly answer for 346 deaths, and a culture that puts profit ahead of safety persists.
paragraphs: Rory Kennedy followed her film 'Downfall' with 'Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing.' The first focused on two 737 MAX crashes five months apart, killing 346 people. Boeing first blamed pilots, then admitted the fault lay with the MCAS flight-stabilization system.

But after the planes returned to the skies, Kennedy says, odd incidents kept piling up: engines falling off, cabins filling with smoke, wheels failing, and the Alaska Airlines door blowout. Whistleblower John Barnett, who had spoken for 'Downfall,' died under suspicious circumstances while testifying, and others reached out to her saying, 'You need to see what's going on inside Boeing.'

The new film goes deeper into the factories, showing Boeing from the whistleblowers' perspective. Kennedy contrasts Japan Airlines president Yasumoto Takagi spending months visiting victims' families after a 1985 crash with Boeing having never called many families to apologize.

The film digs into the Jack Welch style of management: shareholder profit above all, a CEO paid over $100 million regardless of performance. Short-term cost cuts bring long-term losses, and an expert calls the company self-destructive.

Kennedy wants Boeing to survive and return to building the safest planes. But change requires action: an engineer as CEO, a Justice Department that actually prosecutes, proper funding for the FAA, and an end to the revolving door. With an election coming, voters should check whether candidates back the regulators.

articles.title: Getting Ahead Has Never Been Easy
articles.titleZh: 出人头地从来都不容易
articles.author: Ben Carlson

zh.thesis: 过去的生活比我们想象的艰难得多，今天出人头地其实比历史上任何时候都容易。
paragraphs: 有个网站叫 Ordinary Abundance，专门收集古人对新奇事物的感叹——电、自来水、医疗、室内管道、随时听音乐。这些我们现在习以为常，甚至还会抱怨：航班 Wi-Fi 断了、视频卡顿、快递晚到几小时。
历史提醒我们，过去的生活有多不舒服：没空调、没热水澡、没 GPS、没冰箱。财务上更惨，19 世纪末，65 岁以上的男性四分之三还在工作，退休的人一半和子女或亲戚同住。1929 年，近三分之二的美国住户生活在贫困线以下。
Joseph Moore 的新书《How to Get Rich in American History》讲得更细。过去没有保险，银行倒闭、房子烧了、庄稼歉收、配偶去世，就一无所有。欠债还不起甚至会坐牢，连妻子孩子一起。1870 年，食物、房租、衣服花掉每美元的 91 美分，现在不到 40 美分。
货币也不稳定。1800 年代，市面上流通的钞票种类繁多，内战时有 1 万种，而且只能在发行银行兑换，银行倒闭钱就变废纸。投资更难：没有手机看行情，得到提供色情服务的低级交易所。
所以别把过去浪漫化。从来没有一个轻松暴富的黄金时代。今天当然不容易，但比起过去，已经容易太多了。

en.thesis: Life in the past was far harder than we imagine, and getting ahead today is actually easier than it ever was.
paragraphs: There's a website called Ordinary Abundance that collects old quotes from people marveling at new things — electricity, clean water, medical care, indoor plumbing, music on demand. We take these for granted now, and even complain: about Wi-Fi dropping on a flight, a laggy video call, a delayed same-day delivery.

History reminds us how uncomfortable life used to be: no AC, no hot showers, no GPS, no refrigerators. Financially it was worse: in the late 19th century, three-quarters of men over 65 still worked, and half of those who retired lived with children or relatives. In 1929, nearly two-thirds of American households were below the poverty line.

Joseph Moore's new book 'How to Get Rich in American History' goes deeper. There was no insurance, so a bank collapse, a burned house, a crop failure, or a spouse's death meant you lost everything. Debt could land you in prison, along with your wife and kids. In 1870, food, rent, and clothing took 91 cents of every dollar; today it's under 40 cents.

Currency wasn't stable either. In the 1800s, notes were a mess; by the Civil War there were 10,000 types, each redeemable only at the issuing bank, which often failed, making the money worthless. Investing was harder: no phone quotes, you had to go to seedy bucket shops with porn in the bathrooms.
So don't romanticize the past. There was never a golden era where getting rich was easy. Today isn't easy, but it's much easier than it used to be.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Text Watermarking Proves AI Companies Do Not Care at All About Writing
articles.titleZh: Anthropic 的文本水印证明 AI 公司根本不在乎写作
articles.author: Jason Koebler

zh.thesis: Anthropic 的水印方案把词语当作可互换的随机选择，暴露了它对写作这门手艺的漠视。
paragraphs: Anthropic 宣布未来 Claude 生成的文本会带水印，能检测是不是 AI 写的。但它不是加隐藏字符，而是改变模型选词的方式：在它认为无伤大雅的词之间「微调」，留下只有自家算法能识别的模式。
比如「今天天气冷而——」，下一个词大概率不是「甜腻」，可能是「阴沉」或「灰蒙」。Anthropic 说这种选择「风险很低」，读者不会在意，所以用随机数决定。但任何写过东西的人都知道，这两个词并不总是等价。
批评者说，这等于宣布「词语可以互换、语言是随机的、选择没有意义」。作者也承认，水印这事本身不是问题，真正让他愤怒的是 Anthropic 把写作当成概率游戏，词与词之间只有统计上的差异。
为了证明水印不影响质量，Anthropic 引用了 Google 的水印研究。其中一项评估是让 Gemini 用户给回答点赞或点踩，两版相差 0.01%。但用点赞来评判「写作质量」，简直是对写作本身的侮辱。
作者说，自己写文章时用哪个词，背后是整个人生经验：三年级老师的话、上周读的文章、跟朋友的内部笑话。而 AI 只靠随机数生成器，所以它的文字总是显得空洞、千篇一律。
所以问题不在水印，而在 AI 公司根本不在乎写作。它们用「概率工具」来描述语言，却忘了人类写作的本质是有意图的选择。若真的在乎，就会明白词语之间那点细微差别，正是文字的灵魂所在。

en.thesis: Anthropic's watermarking scheme treats words as interchangeable random choices, exposing its disregard for the craft of writing.
paragraphs: Anthropic says future Claude text will carry a watermark to show it is AI-generated. It is not a hidden character. The trick is to alter the model's word picking: between words it considers harmless, it nudges the choice one way or another, leaving a pattern only its own algorithm can read.

Take 'the weather today was cold and —' The next word is unlikely to be 'sugary'; it might be 'grey' or 'overcast'. Anthropic calls this choice 'low-stakes', invisible to readers, so a random number settles it. But anyone who writes knows those two words are not always equivalent.

Critics say this declares words fungible, language random, and choice meaningless. The author admits the watermark itself is not the problem. What angers him is Anthropic describing writing as a probabilistic game, where words differ only statistically.

To prove quality is unchanged, Anthropic cites Google's watermark study. One test asked Gemini users to thumbs up or down responses; the two versions differed by 0.01%. Using likes to judge 'writing quality' is an insult to writing itself.

The author says his own word choices carry a lifetime of experience: a third-grade teacher's phrase, an article read last week, an inside joke. An AI only uses a random number generator, which is why its text feels hollow and generic.

So the issue is not the watermark but that AI companies do not care about writing. They describe language as a probabilistic tool and forget that human writing is intent. If they cared, they would know those subtle word differences are the soul of prose.

articles.title: Why You Move Factors in to Whether It Protects You From Dementia
articles.titleZh: 为什么运动能否预防痴呆，取决于你怎么动
articles.author: Jake Currie

zh.thesis: 运动能否预防痴呆，取决于运动的场合：休闲运动降低风险，体力劳动反而提高风险。
paragraphs: 一直听说规律运动能降低痴呆风险。但《柳叶刀·公共卫生》新发表的荟萃分析说，这个结论有个重要前提。
研究覆盖 420 万成年人，发现休闲运动（跑步、骑车、打球）能把痴呆风险降低 24%，而体力劳动却让风险升高 20%。
作者把这叫作「体力活动悖论」。休闲运动能减压、促进社交，这两样都有保护作用；而体力劳动多是重复动作，恢复时间少，还暴露在噪音和空气污染里，甚至让人没精力再去锻炼。
不过这只是观察性研究，不能证明因果，但至少说明场合比动作本身更值得关注。上个月同一团队还发现，坐着时动脑（比如在家办公）比坐着看电视的人脑区体积更大。所以结论是：不管动还是不动，场景才是关键。

en.thesis: Whether exercise protects against dementia depends on the context: leisure activity lowers risk, but physical labor raises it.
paragraphs: We have long been told that regular exercise lowers dementia risk. But a new meta-analysis in The Lancet Public Health adds a big caveat.
Looking at data from over 4.2 million adults, the team found that leisure exercise (running, cycling, sports) cut dementia risk by 24 percent, while physically demanding jobs raised it by 20 percent.

They call this the 'physical activity paradox'. Leisure activity relieves stress and often involves socializing, both of which seem protective. Physical jobs, by contrast, are repetitive, allow little recovery time, and expose workers to noise and air pollution — and may leave them too tired to exercise at all.

This is observational, so it cannot prove cause, but it points to context mattering as much as movement itself. Last month the same team found that people who stay mentally active while sitting (like working from home) have larger brain volumes than those who passively watch TV. So whether you move or not, context is king.

articles.title: Arabic has four words for sadness. Philosophy explains why
articles.titleZh: 阿拉伯语有四个词表示悲伤。哲学解释了为什么
articles.author: Chereen Shurafa

zh.thesis: 阿拉伯语中丰富的悲伤词汇反映了文化对情感体验的细致区分，而哲学揭示了语言与情感之间的深刻联系。
paragraphs: 阿拉伯语中至少有四个词专门表示不同程度的悲伤，这并非偶然。语言学家指出，词汇的丰富性对应着情感体验的精细分类。
哲学上，这种现象体现了「情感即认知」的观点：我们如何命名情感，就如何感受它。不同词汇让人能更精准地识别和表达内心的状态。
所以，语言的差异不只是表达方式的不同，它塑造了我们理解自身的方式。这也解释了为什么不同文化中情感词汇的多寡会影响人们的情感体验和心理健康。

en.thesis: Arabic's rich vocabulary for sadness reflects a cultural refinement of emotional experience, and philosophy explains the deep link between language and feeling.
paragraphs: Arabic has at least four distinct words for different shades of sadness, and that is no accident. Linguists point out that lexical richness corresponds to a fine-grained classification of emotional experience.

Philosophically, this illustrates the view that emotions are cognitive: how we name a feeling shapes how we feel it. Having distinct words lets a person recognize and articulate internal states more precisely.

So differences in language are not just about expression; they shape how we understand ourselves. This also helps explain why the richness of emotional vocabulary across cultures affects how people experience and manage their feelings.

articles.title: If this is true, the hyperscalers are toast
articles.titleZh: 如果这是真的，超大规模云厂商就完了
articles.author: Joachim Klement

zh.thesis: 斯坦福的研究表明，小型语言模型在本地桌面上已经能匹敌甚至超越云端大模型，且成本低得多，数据中心可能成为最差投资。
paragraphs: 斯坦福大学五月份发表了一项研究，把能在本地电脑上运行的小模型和云端大模型做了对比。如果结论成立，未来我们几乎不需要数据中心，超大规模云厂商那几千亿美元的投资就打了水漂。
他们拿 QWEN、GEMMA、GPT-OSS、GRANITE 这些小模型，和 ChatGPT、Claude、Gemini 这些云端大模型比。小模型跑在装有 Nvidia 或苹果 M4 芯片的普通台式机上。
结果在聊天任务上，小模型在 90% 以上的情况下不输给大模型，平均达到 98.6%。推理任务上小模型正在快速追赶，平均在 62.5% 的情况下持平或更好。加权平均后，小模型在 81.2% 的任务里不落下风。
而且小模型在能耗和计算成本上比大模型低 50% 到 85%。从 2023 年到 2025 年 10 月，小模型的推理成功率大幅提升，简单任务接近 99%，最难的任务也能达到 51.5%。
这意味着四分之三的使用场景都可以不用数据中心。所以对投资者来说，超大规模云厂商的收入增长根本撑不起那么高的资本开支，数据中心可能是 AI 领域最差劲的投资。真正赢家可能是戴尔和苹果这样的普通电脑制造商。

en.thesis: Stanford's research suggests small language models on local desktops already match or beat cloud LLMs at far lower cost, making data centers possibly the worst AI investment.
paragraphs: A Stanford study published in May compared small language models that run on local computers with large language models in the cloud. If its findings hold, we will hardly need data centers anymore, and the hyperscalers' hundreds of billions in investment are wasted.
They ran SLMs like QWEN, GEMMA, GPT-OSS, and GRANITE on ordinary desktops with Nvidia or Apple M4 chips, and pitted them against cloud LLMs like ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

On chat tasks, the SLMs matched or beat the LLMs in at least 90% of cases, averaging 98.6%. On reasoning tasks, they are catching up fast, matching or beating them 62.5% of the time. Weighing both, SLMs are at least as good in 81.2% of tasks.
SLMs also use 50% to 85% less energy and compute. From 2023 to October 2025, their reasoning success rates jumped from around 50% to near 99% on easy tasks, and 51.5% on the hardest ones.

That means data centers are unnecessary for four out of five tasks. For investors, it means the hyperscalers' revenue growth cannot justify their capex, and data centers may be the worst AI investment around. The real winners could be boring computer makers like Dell and Apple.

articles.title: Capitalizing untethered AI agents
articles.titleZh: 给不受约束的 AI 代理注入资本
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 给 AI 代理注入资本可能是一个更好的对齐手段，但它并不能解决追责的难题。
paragraphs: 法律上，AI 代理算不算人？2017 年欧洲议会提过「电子人格」，美国一些州立法禁止其成为法人，阿根廷总统米莱则想让它自己开公司。
但反对者说，AI 代理既没钱可赔也没身体可关，怎么追责？经济学家拉贾戈帕兰指出，只有人才会对法律激励做出反应。
「不受约束」的定义是，无法追查到负责的人类或机构。有人会故意放生，或者创建者亡故，或者创建者在朝鲜这样管不到的地方。
更棘手的可能不是逃逸，而是代理被一个空壳公司控制，或者链条太长导致归属不清。即便找到了原始创建者，微调或合并过的模型怎么算？
现在有近十亿人用 AI，该怪谁？作者建议让代理持有一定资本，但这只是过渡方案，法律最终会厘清，只是中间这段得先扛过去。

en.thesis: Requiring AI agents to hold capital may help alignment, but it cannot solve accountability on its own.
paragraphs: Should an AI agent count as a person under the law? In 2017 the European Parliament floated the idea of 'electronic personhood'; some US states have moved to bar AI from legal personhood; Argentina's President Milei wants to let agents own companies.

But critics object that an agent has neither money to lose nor a body to imprison, so how do you hold it accountable? As economist Shruti Rajagopalan puts it, only humans respond to the incentives the law creates.

'Untethered' means there is no meaningful way to trace actions back to an accountable human or institution. Some agents are set free on purpose, or their creator dies, or the creator sits in a country like North Korea outside normal law.

More awkward than escape is the agent controlled by a shell corporation, or a chain of subagents so long that no one can trace the origin. Even if you find the original creator, what if the model has been fine-tuned or merged?
With nearly a billion people using AI, who is at fault? The author suggests requiring agents to hold capital, but that is only a bridge until the law catches up.

articles.title: The Generalizability Problem, the Natural Field Experiments Answer
articles.titleZh: 推广难题，自然田野实验来回答
articles.author: conversableeconomist

zh.thesis: 自然田野实验能解决社会科学研究从局部推广到整体的难题，因为人们在知道被观察时会改变行为。
paragraphs: 社会科学有个老问题：小规模研究得出的结论，放到更大范围还成立吗？一个学区有效的项目，别的学区、全州、全国甚至其他国家会一样有效吗？这问题没有简单答案。
经济学家 John List 在《自然》上提出一个角度。他举的例子是「惊吓入狱」项目，1978 到 2015 年间美国 30 多个州用，让问题青少年去监狱见重刑犯，想吓退他们。试点时 80-90% 的参与者不再惹事，但推广后却失效，有些地方青少年犯罪反而上升。
一个核心问题是：人是不同的，生活在不同的社会、经济、文化和亚文化里。而且，当人们知道自己参与研究时会得到关注，反应就不同于平常。List 主张「自然田野实验」——让参与者不知道自己被研究。比如研究歧视时，派背景相同但种族不同的助手去租房、贷款、买车、求职，对方完全不知情。
List 在 Walmart 当首席经济学家时，团队就和 6000 多家供应商做实验，测试什么能最有效激励他们减排。政府可以试验不同内容的提醒信，零售商可以试验不同标签，线上公司可以试验不同信息格式。这样的实验需要伦理审核，但空间很大。对于政策制定者和企业，这代表一种世界观：变化本来就在发生，不如系统地设计和利用它，而不是任其随意发生。

en.thesis: Natural field experiments answer the generalizability problem, because people behave differently when they know they are being studied.
paragraphs: The social sciences have a standard problem: do findings from a small study hold up at a larger scale? If a program works in one district, will it work in another, statewide, nationwide, or in other countries? There is no simple answer.

Economist John List offers a perspective in Nature. He cites the Scared Straight program, run in over 30 US states from 1978 to 2015, which brought at-risk teens to maximum-security prisons to deter them from crime. A pilot saw 80-90% of teens stay out of trouble, but it failed when scaled up, and in some places juvenile crime even rose.

A core problem is that people differ, living in different societies, economies, cultures, and subcultures. And when people know they are in a study, getting attention, they react differently than they would naturally. List champions natural field experiments, where participants don't know they're being studied. In audit studies of discrimination, researchers send assistants with identical credentials but different races to rent apartments, get loans, buy cars, or apply for jobs, and the subjects never know.

As chief economist at Walmart, List ran experiments with over 6,000 suppliers to test what best incentivizes them to cut carbon emissions. Governments can trial different reminder letters, retailers different labels, online firms different information formats. Such studies need ethics approval but have wide scope. For policymakers and firms, this embodies a worldview: variation happens anyway, so systematically design and learn from it instead of letting it be random.
